Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says paying more under California’s proposed billionaire tax would be “a privilege.”

The measure is a one-time 5% tax on residents worth more than $1.1B as of Jan. 1, 2026, payable over five years. Asked by CBS News’ Jo Ling Kent about a potential bill of about $8B over five years, Huang said: “The more you make, the more taxes you pay. I’m okay with that.” He added, “I’m not afraid of paying taxes. I’m just afraid of being poor.”

He made the same point at the Milken Institute’s Global Conference in May: “I prefer lower taxes, but whatever they decide to ask me to pay, I’ll pay.” He said he and his wife Lori chose California for Stanford, its companies and its culture, not for its tax rates.

His stance stands out as some wealthy residents leave the state ahead of Prop 40 on November 3rd.
